Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks, part of Strand 9 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Which punctuation marks do you know? 2. Why do we punctuate sentences?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 9.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination is enriched as the learner develops and displays posters and charts in the classroom for

peers to review.

• Learning to Learn is developed as the learner searches for information on the internet and learns surfing skills.

Values:
Responsibility is developed as the learner creates and displays charts using different types of sentences and punctuates

them correctly.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Health Education is enhanced as the learner interacts with material on common communicable diseases both offline

and online.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Punctuation marks are used in all areas of learning as the learner takes down notes. Kiswahili in particular is an area

that the learner can apply this concept, as it teaches on punctuation as a skill.
